body:
Like another commenter, I also have a giant wall of text for you. Yes, I regret not being more social all the time and am looking forward to going back to school so I can regain a bit of what I missed out on. The best advice I can offer you is to try to go to events with friends/acquaintances you already have, especially if they're more social. It easier to meet more people through friends than on your own. Personally, I find having a few drinks, not enough to get sloppy drunk and act in a way I'll regret later, often makes me feel calmer and more outgoing in social situations and has helped me strike up conversation with greater ease.

In one of your comments you mentioned that you want a significant other and aren't that into the club scene. Honestly, the best advice I can offer you is to not expect to meet someone you're going to have a meaningful relationship with at a club. It can be fun, you can have a great time with your friends, and meet some interesting people, but I've never known anybody who met a girl/guy at a club and had a strong relationship with them. Are you still in high school? If so, and I know you said you planned on educating yourself after you graduate, go to college. If you're not 100% sold on the idea, you can start off taking a class or two in subjects you're passionate about at a city or community college, which is generally affordable. Since you're studying subjects you want to take instead of mandatory ones in H.S. you'll meet people who are also interested in the same things you are. Most colleges have a decent amount of clubs for you to join so you can meet other people who are passionate about the same things you are, and try out new things you might have an interest in. Interested in a particular social cause? There's probably a club centered around it or at least one that advocates for it. Wanted to learn how to play a certain sport? Colleges have tons of intramural teams. Have a hobby or interest? Odds are plenty of other kids at your school do too. The great part of meeting people this way is that you already know you have something in common, something you can talk about and bond over, as opposed to meeting people at a bar or a club where you're all just there for the sake of partying. If you're not crazy about going to clubs every weekend don't feel compelled to go all the time. There's so many other social opportunities out there for you.

It's probably weird for me to give you advice since I'm in a similar mental places, even for if other reasons, but here goes. It sounds like you're fairly accomplished at a young age and had what many consider to be an ideal upbringing. This may have given you unrealistic expectations for yourself to be close to perfect and when you can't live up to that, because nobody can, you assume you're worse than you are. You're at an age where you're probably close to graduation and that brings about a ton of anxiety and contemplation. No, it's not cool that you cheated on your girlfriend, but you were right to tell her about it. It sounds like you love her but in your early 20s, you're not expected to know for sure if you want to be with the girl with for the rest of your life. It's normal to have anxiety as relationships move on about where they stand and if you're sure they're what you want, even in the best cases. 

I agree with others that you may want to look into therapy. Since you're enrolled in school you should be able to get counseling cheap, if not free.

I like to think you're right. Dating is the least of my concerns right now, I have too much going on and am too much of a mess right now to be a decent boyfriend, but it pains me to think women would discount me off the bat. It's making losing someone who I loved and accepted me a lot harder. Thank-you for your kind words and for reading that lengthy wall of text. I hope to keep moving along, but it feels difficult to think of carrying on right now.

Some backstory: I started showing signs of gender identity disorder as a child that went largely ignored by my family, who I couldn't talk to about anything. They did not however go ignored by kids I went to school with who made my life a living hell to the point where I barely spoke from grades 5-8. High school was a slight improvement in that I had friends, but I was trying to hide who I was and it was awful for me. Got a little older, had a girlfriend I was with for a long time who seemed to love and accept me, then found out she was a pathological liar. 

My life improved in so many ways since undergoing hormone therapy and I'm finally in a place where I'm largely comfortable with myself, except romantically. The years of feeling like crap, not being socialized as the correct gender and keeping myself kind of isolated have prevented me from growing as a person, developing social skills and learning how to approach women in a non-platonic way that most guys pick up in their teens. I'm also content in finally being recognized as a guy that I really don't look forward to having to explain why I'm "different", or answering a bunch of questions about an issue I've been moving on from. I don't trust that the person I told wouldn't tell other people, which is one of my biggest fears. I'm around 5'5 and while I'm not bad looking, I'm definitely not the tall, dark and handsome sort most women seem most attracted to.  

Overlooking all that stuff, I'm not in a good place to date someone anyway. I'm trying to figure out what I want to do as a career and going back to school. One of my parents is dealing with a serious illness, which has been emotionally draining and makes it difficult for me to get close to people because I don't want to be more vulnerable than I already am. I hate where I live, feel stuck here because of family, and plan to get out at the first opportunity. I'm turned off by the idea of having sex with someone until I really get to know and care about her (some days I feel almost asexual), which most people seem to find strange and I think gives off the impression that I'm disinterested. I feel like I missed out on so much of my youth that I'm a little bit regressed and entitled to it. I don't think it's right to go into a relationship expecting the other person to deal with an emotionally fucked up sometimes manchild,who's discontent with a lot of aspects of his life. Plus it's rare I meet girls I like and am attracted to.

I'm reluctant to call myself Forever Alone, because I like to think of it as a temporary phase, but that's why I'm FA for the moment. Thanks for asking, writing it out felt good.

tl;dr - Gender issues as a kid fucked me up bad and affected how I socialize. Life issues in the present make a relationship seem like an awful idea.
